_readme.purpose: Language-neutral accept/reject contract for the internal-redirect validator (issue #4305). Two implementations of ONE security ruleset read this file, so a rule relaxed on one side fails a test instead of silently producing an open redirect or a silently-dropped journey.
_readme.scope: STRING inputs only. Type-level cases are not portable across languages and stay in the per-language specs: Ruby keeps nil/Integer/Array/Hash and the force-encoded invalid-UTF-8 String; TypeScript keeps undefined/null/number/object/array. Everything expressible as a JSON string — control characters included, via \u escapes — belongs HERE.

how_to_read_a_case.id: stable, unique slug; both suites put it in the test name so a failure names the case
how_to_read_a_case.group: the reason this case exists. Both suites nest their generated examples under it, so the test output reads as a taxonomy of the ruleset rather than a flat list of strings.
how_to_read_a_case.input: the exact string handed to the validator
how_to_read_a_case.expected: the boolean BOTH validators must return
how_to_read_a_case.note: optional; present whenever the verdict is not obvious from the input alone

how_to_add_a_case: Append an object to `cases` with a stable, unique `id` and an existing (or new) `group`.
Add a `note` whenever the verdict is not obvious from the input alone.

Run BOTH suites: `bundle exec rspec spec/unit/onetime/utils/redirect_paths_spec.rb` and `pnpm vitest run src/tests/utils/redirect.spec.ts`. A case that passes on one side and fails on the other is a real parity bug — fix the lagging validator, do not delete the case.
_readme.when_in_doubt: This is a security validator. If the correct verdict for a new case is unclear, the answer is `false`.
